ai_show_review.summary: Strong Candyman vocals, soaring Easy Wind jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The set delivers a high‑energy Easy Wind and a slowed‑down Candyman that showcases Jerry’s mesmerizing voice. Brokedown Palace and Casey Jones also stand out, though the matrix broadcast’s mix is uneven.
ai_show_review.review:
On August 30 1970 the Dead slipped into KQED Studios for a brief studio set that feels more like a radio special than a concert. While the performance runs short, it contains several gems: a driving Easy Wind that lets Jerry stretch his guitar, a tender Candyman where his vocal delivery is described as “mesmerizing,” and a plaintive Brokedown Palace that further highlights his voice. Casey Jones adds its usual punch, and Uncle John’s Band rounds out the set despite the limited time.

Two recordings survive. The matrix broadcast (gd70-08-30.fm.jupile.12762.sbeok.shnf) is only “fair” in fidelity—muddy spots and a low‑mixed bass—but it captures the core of the performance and remains clearer than many contemporary video tapes. The soundboard tape (gd1970-08-30.sbd.backus.12750.sbeok.shnf) suffers from muffled, sluggish mixing that renders most of the set unlistenable, leaving only Candyman as a faint highlight. For anyone curious about this rare studio outing, the matrix broadcast is the recommended source.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality matrix broadcast that, despite uneven mixing, captures the key highlights (Easy Wind, Candyman, Brokedown Palace) more clearly than the poor soundboard tape.

key_highlights: High‑energy Easy Wind jam showcases Jerry’s guitar fire.
Candyman features a mesmerizing vocal performance by Jerry.
Brokedown Palace delivers emotive vocals and acoustic texture.
Casey Jones provides classic driving momentum despite mixed audio.

band_performance.Jerry: His vocals are a highlight on Candyman and Brokedown Palace, with reviewers calling his voice mesmerizing.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is mixed too low in the matrix broadcast, which mutes his usual presence.
